MOD_VOY_ITEM_PITCH_DESC: Tar sweated out of logs by a slow fire. With logs, it repairs a ship's hull on the Voyage page. Burning any logs in Firemaking makes it now and then, and the better the logs, the more often.
MOD_VOY_ITEM_PROSPECTORS_NOTES_DESC: A prospector's notes on where one ore runs. Use it in the Captain's Journal (Resources, Chart a country) to chart the whole country of one Mining rock.
MOD_VOY_ITEM_FORESTERS_SURVEY_DESC: A forester's survey of where one tree grows. Use it in the Captain's Journal (Resources, Chart a country) to chart the whole country of one Woodcutting tree.
MOD_VOY_ITEM_ANGLERS_LOG_DESC: An angler's log of where one fish bites. Use it in the Captain's Journal (Resources, Chart a country) to chart the whole country of one Fishing spot.
MOD_VOY_ITEM_FARMERS_ALMANAC_DESC: A farmer's almanac of where one crop takes. Use it in the Captain's Journal (Resources, Chart a country) to chart the whole country of one Farming seed.
MOD_VOY_ITEM_FENCES_LEDGER_DESC: A fence's ledger of where one mark can be found. Use it in the Captain's Journal (Resources, Chart a country) to chart the whole country of one Thieving target.
MOD_VOY_ITEM_STAR_CHART_DESC: A star chart of where one constellation stands clear. Use it in the Captain's Journal (Resources, Chart a country) to chart the whole country of one Astrology constellation.
MOD_VOY_MILESTONE_1: Compass: how close and which way
MOD_VOY_MILESTONE_3: Compass: the name of the place
MOD_VOY_SETTING_STRICTNESS_HINT_STRICT: Strict: gathering needs terrain, crafting needs a workshop or town.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_STRICTNESS_HINT_RELAXED: Relaxed: gathering keeps to its terrain and Firemaking and Cooking to dry land; other crafts work anywhere.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_OVERLAY_HINT: Tint surveyed hexes by terrain on the Cartography map.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_RULES_HINT: Off: nothing is locked by location; the overlay and the panel stay.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_ZONES_HINT: Each ore, tree, fish, crop, thieving target and constellation is found only in some places: copper in dry red country, salmon in cold rivers, the northern stars in the north.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_COMBAT_HINT: Fight only where the combat area is on the map, or right next to it. Dungeons and strongholds too.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_TRADE_HINT: Sell and buy only in or next to a town, port or market.
MOD_VOY_NOTICE_TABLE_MISMATCH: Voyage: the map differs from the terrain table. Voyage rules are off until the mod is updated.
MOD_VOY_HULL_BLURB_DINGHY: A small rowing boat. It stays within 2 hexes of land and you can board or leave it on any coast.
MOD_VOY_HULL_BLURB_LONGBOAT: A bigger rowing boat with a short mast. It stays within 4 hexes of land and you can board or leave it on any coast, the Cursed Isle included.
MOD_VOY_HULL_BLURB_GALLEON: A three-masted ship of the line. She sails any sea, however far from land and under cloud too, and ties up only at ports. Your small boat rides aboard and rows you ashore anywhere else.
MOD_VOY_HULL_BLURB_BRIG: A two-masted sailing ship. She sails up to 5 hexes from land, under cloud too, and ties up only at ports. Your small boat rides aboard and rows you ashore anywhere else.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_BLOCK_RULES_OFF: Voyage rules are off: turn them on in the mod settings (Voyage rules) to build a ship.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_BLOCK_NOT_COAST: Stand on a coast hex, next to water you have surveyed, to launch it.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_BLOCK_NO_MATERIALS: Something is short: a cost in red is what you lack, with what you have in brackets.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_BUILT: Your dinghy is in the water. Step onto it to board.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_UPGRADED: Your ${hull} is ready at the quay. The hold kept its cargo.
MOD_VOY_UPGRADE_BLOCK_PORT: Built at a port: sail your ${hull} to one and stand on the port or next to it.
MOD_VOY_UPGRADE_BLOCK_QUAY: Bring your ${hull} to the quay: it must be on your hex or next to it.
MOD_VOY_UPGRADE_BLOCK_COST: Something is short: a cost in red is what you lack, with what you have in brackets.
MOD_VOY_BRIG_BLOCK_PORT: Bought at a port: stand on the port or next to it.
MOD_VOY_BRIG_BLOCK_QUAY: This port has no open water beside it for a brig to tie up at. Try another port.
MOD_VOY_BRIG_BOUGHT: Your brig is tied up at the quay. Step aboard and she takes the open sea; your small boat rides on her deck.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_NOTICE_AT_SEA: You are out on the water, so the boat under you is now your dinghy.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_NOTICE_OVERSEAS: The boat you hired to get here is yours now: your dinghy is moored on the nearest coast of this land.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_NEED_BOAT_WATER: You need a ship to go on the water. Build a dinghy on the Voyage page.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_NEED_BOAT_LAND: No way there on foot. You need a ship: build a dinghy on the Voyage page.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_ISLAND_LOCKED: Your ${hull} can't land on ${island}: it needs a ${needed}.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_TOO_FAR: Too far out for your ${hull}: it keeps within ${reach} hexes of a coast it can land on.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_FROZEN: Your ${hull} is frozen in: it waits for the thaw.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_MOORED: No way there on foot. Your ${hull} is moored ${where}; walk to it to sail.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_OTHER_WATER: Your ${hull} can't get there: this water doesn't connect to the sea it is on.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_OUT_OF_REACH: Your ${hull} can't get there: it keeps within ${reach} hexes of land.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_DRAG: Drag the title to move this block
MOD_VOY_PAGE_RESET_LAYOUT_HINT: Every block back where it started, all unfolded
MOD_VOY_PAGE_NO_SHIP: The ship isn't available: the Voyage skill didn't load. Check the console for a [Voyage] error.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_NO_SHIP_YET: No ship yet. You travel on foot.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_BUILD_HINT: It goes into the water next to you.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_UPGRADE_HINT: It replaces your ${old} at full condition.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_BRIG_COST: The brig: bought at a port
MOD_VOY_PAGE_BRIG_HINT: She ties up beside this port. Your boat stays yours and rides aboard.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_RULES_OFF: Voyage rules are off: you can walk on the water, and your ship follows when you step onto the sea. Turn them on in the mod settings.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_STAT_VISITED: Different hexes you have stood on
MOD_VOY_PAGE_STAT_DISCOUNT: Travel costs cut by your Voyage level
MOD_VOY_PAGE_FUTURE_SAVE: This save comes from a newer Voyage build: progress is kept but not counted here.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_COMPASS_STAGE_3: Also the name of the place
MOD_VOY_PAGE_COMPASS_SHOP: The shop sells another under Voyage.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_LAND_SHOP: Opens the shop, where the next mount is sold
MOD_VOY_PAGE_SIGN_SHOP: Opens the shop, where the Crossroads Sign is sold
MOD_VOY_PAGE_SIGN_LOOK: Look for a special place that gives buffs while you stand there, and plant the sign on it
MOD_VOY_PAGE_SIGN_LOCATE: Show the sign on the map
MOD_VOY_PANEL_SIGN_CAN_PLACE: plant it here to carry this place's buffs with you
MOD_VOY_GATE_NEAREST_GRACE: Nearest place it works: ${where}, next to ${match}.
MOD_VOY_GATE_NONE_KNOWN: You know of no ${need} yet. Survey the hexes around you in Cartography to find one.
MOD_VOY_GATE_AREA_STAND: You must stand on ${name} or next to it to fight there.
MOD_VOY_GATE_AREA_HERE: From here you can fight in ${names}.
MOD_VOY_ZONE_NEEDS: ${name} is not found here. Look around ${need}.
MOD_VOY_ZONE_NONE_KNOWN: No place for it is known yet: survey more of the map.
MOD_VOY_ZONE_STOPPED: ${name} stopped: it is not found here.
MOD_VOY_ZONE_SKIPPED: Not planted, they don't grow here: ${names}.
MOD_VOY_ZONE_SKY_NEEDS: ${name} cannot be seen from here. It shows ${where}.
MOD_VOY_ZONE_SKY_DARK: Stars need a dark, open sky: not next to a town, not under a forest.
MOD_VOY_ZONE_LAT_NORTH: in the north, at row ${row} or further north
MOD_VOY_ZONE_LAT_SOUTH: in the south, at row ${row} or further south
MOD_VOY_GATE_AREA_UNKNOWN: You do not know where ${name} is yet. Survey the hexes around you in Cartography to find it.
MOD_VOY_GATE_TRADE_ONLY_SELL: You can sell only in a town, port or market, or next to one.
MOD_VOY_GATE_TRADE_ONLY_BUY: You can buy only in a town, port or market, or next to one.
MOD_VOY_GATE_TRADE_NONE_KNOWN: You know of no trading place yet. Survey the hexes around you in Cartography to find one.
MOD_VOY_GATE_TRADE_TITLE: No one to trade with here
MOD_VOY_GATE_STOPPED: ${name} stopped: it does not work here.
MOD_VOY_FOLK_NO_PLACE: No place yet: picking this Folk for a skill puts it on your hex.
MOD_VOY_CREW_NO_VESSEL: No vessel yet: Folks can walk with you, but none can cross the water.
MOD_VOY_CREW_EATS_TIP: Each hex this ${rank} eats ${pct}% of the food you eat. Fuel: as much as you.
MOD_VOY_CREW_LASTS_TIP: On empty stores every hex costs this Folk ${hp} HP. Stock up, or put it ashore.
MOD_VOY_CREW_NEAR_NONE: Folks within a hex of you can come along.
MOD_VOY_CREW_COME_STOPS: A Folk who comes along stops its work.
MOD_VOY_CREW_WORK_NONE: No skill a Folk can do works on this hex.
MOD_VOY_CREW_HINT: Every Folk with you eats by its rank (a Journeyman as much as you) and burns fuel like you. On empty stores each loses HP every hex, and can die.
MOD_VOY_CREW_BUSY_VOYAGE: The crew can't change while a voyage is under way.
MOD_VOY_CREW_BUSY_ADRIFT: The crew can't change while you are adrift.
MOD_VOY_CREW_ASHORE_SEA: Folks are put ashore on land: a coast or a port.
MOD_VOY_CREW_REFUSE_BERTHS: The ${hull} has ${berths} berths for your ${crew} Folks. Put some ashore first.
MOD_VOY_STORES_PATH_COST_TIP_CREW_ONE: Provisions: what this trip eats, for you and 1 Folk
MOD_VOY_STORES_PATH_COST_TIP_CREW: Provisions: what this trip eats, for you and ${count} Folks
MOD_VOY_CLOCK_COST_CREW_TIP: The food and fuel above feed the Folks with you too.
MOD_VOY_HELP_CREW_WHAT: Folks from Worker Folks can come along with you. A Folk with you doesn't work, doesn't heal, and earns no Voyage XP until you put it ashore.
MOD_VOY_HELP_CREW_BERTHS: On land the crew walks. On the water each Folk needs a berth in the vessel you sail; a crew too big for it waits until you put some ashore.
MOD_VOY_HELP_CREW_EATS: Every Folk eats from the stores by its rank: a Journeyman as much as you, a lower rank less, a higher one more. Each burns as much fuel as you do.
MOD_VOY_HELP_CREW_HUNGER: On empty stores every Folk with you loses ${pct}% of its max HP each hex. It can't eat its own food on the road, and hunger can kill it.
MOD_VOY_HELP_CREW_BLOCK: The Crew block shows each Folk's health, and for each one with you how many hexes of empty stores it would live through.
MOD_VOY_HELP_CREW_ASHORE: Put a Folk ashore on land and pick its work there: it stays on that hex, as any Folk does.
MOD_VOY_HELP_CREW_FIXED: The crew changes only while you stand still: not on a voyage under way, not adrift.
MOD_VOY_CREW_NO_BERTH_ONE: The ${hull} has 1 berth, and it is taken.
MOD_VOY_CREW_REFUSE_BERTHS_ONE: The ${hull} has 1 berth for your ${crew} Folks. Put some ashore first.
MOD_VOY_WALK_BUSY: ${name} is walking to ${to}: wait until it arrives, or stop it from the Crew on the Voyage page.
MOD_VOY_WALK_SEND_TEXT: ${name} walks there alone, on foot, and starts the work when it arrives.
MOD_VOY_WALK_NO_PLACES: The Journal has no place for this yet.
MOD_VOY_WALK_NO_WORKS: The Journal has found no resource yet. Work a resource somewhere and the Journal writes down where; then a Folk can be sent there.
MOD_VOY_WALK_PACK_HINT: Its food (by its rank) and fuel for the road come out of your stores when it sets off.
MOD_VOY_WALK_PICK_PLACE: Pick a place it can reach.
MOD_VOY_WALK_ACROSS_WATER: No road over land you know: take ${name} along in a berth.
MOD_VOY_WALK_THERE_ALREADY: ${name} is there already: give it the work on the skill's page.
MOD_VOY_WALK_SHORT: The stores are short: the road takes ${amounts}.
MOD_VOY_WALK_STOP_TEXT: ${name} stops on the hex it has reached on the way to ${to} and waits there with no work. The food packed for the rest of the road is lost.
MOD_VOY_WALK_STOPPED: ${name} stops on ${where} and waits there with no work.
MOD_VOY_WALK_ARRIVED_WORKS: ${name} has arrived at ${where} and started on ${skill}.
MOD_VOY_WALK_ARRIVED_HOLDS: ${name} has arrived at ${where} and holds ${skill}: start it on the skill's page.
MOD_VOY_WALK_ARRIVED_CANT: ${name} has arrived at ${where} and waits there with no work. ${why}
MOD_VOY_WALK_TAKES: ${holder} has ${skill} now: ${name} takes it over on arrival.
MOD_VOY_STORES_PATH_FUEL_TIP_CREW_ONE: Fuel this trip burns, for you and 1 Folk
MOD_VOY_STORES_PATH_FUEL_TIP_CREW: Fuel this trip burns, for you and ${count} Folks
MOD_VOY_FOLK_JOB_KEPT: Its ${skill} job waits: you can give it back from anywhere
MOD_VOY_GATE_FIGHT_LEFT: You left ${name}: the fight is over.
MOD_VOY_GATE_FIGHT_OUT_OF_REACH: ${name} is out of reach from here: the fight is over.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_ZONE_NONE_HERE: None of it is found here.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_SKY_NONE_ROW: None of your constellations can be seen from here: another place shows other stars.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_ZONE_NEVER: ${skill} is locked here: none of it is found here.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_SKY_NONE: ${skill} is locked here: none of your constellations can be seen. Another place shows other stars.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_STRANDED_HINT: You cannot afford the road to a place where you can earn GP.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_TRADE_OK_HINT: You can sell and buy here.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_TRADER_HERE_HINT: Selling works here at half price until you can afford the road to a trading place.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_TRADER_HERE: A wandering trader is here (half price)
MOD_VOY_PANEL_NO_TRADE_HINT: Sell, buy and trade only in a town, port or market, or next to one.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_COMBAT_HINT: Combat areas you can enter from this hex: you stand on the area or right next to it.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_VESSEL_FOLD: Fold the vessel, stores and crew
MOD_VOY_PANEL_VESSEL_UNFOLD: Show the vessel, stores and crew
MOD_VOY_MINI_CREW_HUNGRY: The food is out: every hex costs them HP.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_TABLE_MISMATCH: Map differs from the terrain table: rules off.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_UNTUCK: Tap to show it again as it was.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_HOLD_TUCK: Press and hold to shrink it to a small button.
MOD_VOY_TRADER_LEFT_BEHIND: You leave the wandering trader behind.
MOD_VOY_TRADER_MOVES_ON: The wandering trader moves on: you can afford the road now.
MOD_VOY_TRADER_ARRIVES: Looks like you're stranded here. Good timing: a wandering trader is just passing by.
MOD_VOY_TRADER_HALF_PRICE: He looks over your goods and offers half of what a market would pay. You see his eyes spark for a moment: he knows you have no other choice.
MOD_VOY_TRADER_STAYS: He stays until you can afford the road to a trading place.
MOD_VOY_TRADER_SPARES_COMBAT: You have nothing worth selling. He sighs and spares you ${gp} GP, just enough for the road to ${area}: the hex at (${at}), ${hexes} ${dir}. "Fight for your coin there," he says, "and sell what you find."
MOD_VOY_TRADER_SPARES_STEP: You have nothing worth selling, and nothing grows or swims here. He sighs and spares you ${gp} GP, just enough for one step ${dir}.
MOD_VOY_TRADER_NO_ROAD: You have nothing worth selling, and he has no road to point you to. He shrugs and walks on.
MOD_VOY_UNLOCK_BOTH: Voyage unlocked Cartography and the Voyage skill for you. Your next skill unlock costs two steps more.
MOD_VOY_UNLOCK_CARTOGRAPHY: Voyage unlocked Cartography for you. Your next skill unlock costs one step more.
MOD_VOY_UNLOCK_VOYAGE: Voyage unlocked the Voyage skill for you. Your next skill unlock costs one step more.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_PROVISIONS_HINT: Every hex costs food from the stores you load on the Voyage page, and fuel for the campfire on land; hard and cold ground burn more. Sailing wears the hull, which you repair with logs and Pitch. Easy ground stays walkable on empty stores.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_NIGHT_HINT: From 21:00 to 05:00 on your own clock, spare fuel lights the way, and each lit hex gives 25% more Voyage XP. Light only burns fuel the trip doesn't need, so night is never worse than day. Off: it is always day.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_WEATHER_HINT: Township's seasons on the map: cold land burns more fuel, hot land asks more rations, Fall loads food better, and in Winter the sea by the Snowlands freezes. The journal has the table. Off: no weather at all.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_NIGHT_SHIFT_HINT: From -12 to 12. With 2, night runs from 23:00 to 07:00.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_CENTRE_KEY_HINT: One letter or digit, G by default. On the Cartography page it does what the map's home button does. Leave it empty to turn it off.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_JOURNAL_KEY_HINT: One letter or digit, J by default. Opens the Captain's Journal from any page and closes it again. Leave it empty to turn it off.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_MAP_MOTION_HINT: While a voyage is under way the traveller walks and the vessel you are in rolls on the swell. Off: they stand still.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_BOOK_OPENING: Open the journal by its cover
MOD_VOY_SETTING_BOOK_OPENING_HINT: The cover swings open and a few pages turn every time the journal opens. Off: only the first time, once per character.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_MAP_KEY_HINT: One letter or digit, M by default. Opens the Cartography page (the world map) from any other page. Leave it empty to turn it off.
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_FOOD: This trip needs ${need} HP of food; your stores hold ${have}. The food runs out ${hexes} along, entering ${terrain}.
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_FUEL: This trip needs ${need} fuel for campfires and lanterns; your stores hold ${have}. The fuel runs out ${hexes} along, entering ${terrain}.
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_HOP: Sailing ${hexes} hexes to that port needs ${need} HP of food; your stores hold ${have}.
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_ASHORE: This voyage needs ${trip} HP of food and would leave ${left} HP at sea, short of the ${need} HP for the way back to the coast (your stores hold ${have}).
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_HINT_SEA: Sail a shorter way, or stock up on food on the Voyage page at a port, town, market, farm, village or camp.
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_HINT: Stock up on food and fuel on the Voyage page at a port, town, market, farm, village or camp. Easy ground (Grasslands, Kingslands, Beach, Desert, Swamplands) can still be walked on empty stores, for no Voyage XP.
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_HULL: Your ${hull}'s hull is at ${cond}%. This voyage would wear it ${need}%, and it gives out ${hexes} along.
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_DEEP: Your ${hull}'s hull is at ${cond}%. Below ${worn}% it keeps out of deep water (3 or more hexes from land).
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_HULL_ASHORE: This voyage would leave your ${hull}'s hull too worn to get back ashore. Keep ${need}% for the way to the coast; it is at ${cond}% now.
MOD_VOY_STORES_REFUSE_HULL_HINT: Repair it on the Voyage page with logs and Pitch: beach it on a coast and stand on it or next to it. A step closer to the coast always goes, however worn the hull.
MOD_VOY_STORES_RESCUE: A wandering trader knows the way out. He walks you to easier ground or a place to load, ${hexes} ${dir}: nothing from your stores and no Voyage XP for it, the road's GP as usual if you have it.
MOD_VOY_STORES_PATH_SHORT: Not enough to go: stock up at a port, town, market, farm, village or camp.
MOD_VOY_STORES_PATH_ASHORE: Keep food to get back ashore.
MOD_VOY_STORES_PATH_HUNGRY: ${hexes} walked hungry, for no Voyage XP.
MOD_VOY_STORES_PATH_HULL: The hull is too worn for this.
MOD_VOY_STORES_PATH_LIGHT_TIP: Night: spare fuel lights the lanterns, and every lit hex gives +${bonus}% Voyage XP
MOD_VOY_STORES_PATH_WX_TIP: The weather on the way (${season}): the coldest or hottest land hex, and what its degrees do
MOD_VOY_STORES_KIT: Your stores are packed for the road: ${amounts}. Stock up on the Voyage page at a port, town, market, farm, village or camp.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_STORES_OFF: Provisions are off (setting or map rules): moves take nothing from the stores.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_STORES_NO_LOADING: Nothing to load here: stores load at a port, town, market, farm, village or camp.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_STORES_LOADING: Loading at ${place}: food costs ${food} of its usual price, fuel ${fuel}.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_STORES_NO_FOOD: No food in your bank. Cook some, or buy it at a market.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_STORES_NO_FUEL: Nothing to burn in your bank: bring logs, coal or charcoal.
MOD_VOY_PAGE_NIGHT_OFF: Night is off (setting): it is always day.
MOD_VOY_HULL_BLOCK_BEACH: Beach your ${hull} first: it must be next to land, with you on it or beside it.
MOD_VOY_HULL_BLOCK_DECK: Your ${hull} rides on your ${ship}'s deck: go aboard the ${ship} to mend it.
MOD_VOY_HULL_BLOCK_PORT: Repaired at a port: bring your ${hull} to one, with you on it or beside it.
MOD_VOY_HULL_BLOCK_MATERIALS: Needs ${logs} logs and ${pitch} Pitch for every ${step}%.

MOD_VOY_HOLD_FULL_PAGE: The hold is full: take something out, or stow more of a kind already aboard.
MOD_VOY_HOLD_AWAY: Your ${hull} is ${where}: stand on it or next to it to use the hold.
MOD_VOY_HOLD_FULL: Your ${hull}'s hold has no free slot.
MOD_VOY_HOLD_BANK_FULL: Your bank has no free slot for it.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_STORES_LOAD_HINT: You can stock up here: food at ${food}% of its usual price, fuel at ${fuel}%.
MOD_VOY_WX_NO_TOWN: Spring stays until you reach a town.

MOD_VOY_WX_FROZE: The sea within two hexes of the Snowlands froze.
MOD_VOY_WX_THAWED: The ice round the Snowlands thawed.
MOD_VOY_WX_ALL_NIGHT: Night all season: spare fuel lights the way and lit hexes give more Voyage XP.
MOD_VOY_WX_HARVEST: Harvest: food loads a quarter better wherever it loads.
MOD_VOY_WX_LEMON: Rations at sea go a quarter further.
MOD_VOY_WX_FROZEN_IN: Your ${hull} is frozen in at ${where} until the thaw.
MOD_VOY_WX_ASHORE: The ice thawed under you: brought ashore at ${where}.
MOD_VOY_WX_WHY_ICE: the ice changed on the way
MOD_VOY_WX_PANEL_FROZEN: Your ${hull} is frozen in until the thaw.
MOD_VOY_WX_PANEL_HINT: On land, cold burns more fuel and heat asks more rations. The sea feels neither. The journal has the table.

MOD_VOY_STORM_PUSHED: Sailed through a storm: ${wear}% hull wear, pushed a hex ${side} and back.

MOD_VOY_WX_PAGE_FALL: The cold comes down to the Cursedlands. Harvest: food loads a quarter better wherever it loads.
MOD_VOY_WX_PAGE_WINTER: Snowlands and Mountain are bitter: half again the fuel, and slower. The sea by the Snowlands freezes.
MOD_VOY_WX_PAGE_NIGHTFALL: Night all season, at Spring's degrees.
MOD_VOY_WX_PAGE_ECLIPSE: Night all season, at Spring's degrees.
MOD_VOY_WX_PAGE_LEMON: Rations at sea go a quarter further, at Spring's degrees.
MOD_VOY_WX_PAGE_DARKNESS: Night all season, at Spring's degrees.
MOD_VOY_PANEL_NIGHT_HINT: At night, spare fuel lights the way: ${land} for each land hex, ${sea} for each sea hex. Each lit hex gives ${bonus}% more Voyage XP. Light only burns fuel the trip doesn't need.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_HOP_NO_BOAT: Fast travel between ports is sailing: bring your ship to this port's quay first.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_PATH_HOP_AWAY: Fast travel is sailing: bring your ${hull} to this port's quay first (it is ${where}).
MOD_VOY_PANEL_HUNGRY_HINT: Your stores can't pay the way to easier ground or a place to load. A wandering trader will walk you out.
MOD_VOY_HELP_FUEL_WHY: Fuel is for the campfire, so by day the sea costs food only. By night every hex burns fuel for light, the lanterns at sea included (see Night).
MOD_VOY_HELP_CREW_COSTS: Folks with you eat by rank, from half your food (a Trainee) to half again (a Foreman), and each burns as much fuel as you. Night light is yours alone.
MOD_VOY_HELP_ROOM_LEVEL: At Voyage level ${level}. Every level adds ${food} HP of food and ${fuel} fuel.
MOD_VOY_HELP_LOAD_WHERE: Stock up on food and fuel from your bank standing on a place or next to it. The table shows how much of it reaches the stores.
MOD_VOY_HELP_NIGHT_XP: A lit hex gives ${bonus}% more Voyage XP.
MOD_VOY_HELP_NIGHT_STARS: Very rarely a lit sea hex turns up a Steersman's Chart: read it from the bank to chart the sea you are on.
MOD_VOY_HELP_WORN: Below ${worn}% it keeps out of deep water.
MOD_VOY_HELP_WORN_THROUGH: Worn through, it only heads for the coast.
MOD_VOY_HELP_PITCH: Pitch comes from Firemaking: ${chance}% a log at level 1, more with better logs.
MOD_VOY_HELP_HOLD_SLOTS: The hold keeps bank items aboard, bank-style: one kind of item a slot, in any amount.
MOD_VOY_HELP_HOLD_WHERE: Stand on your ship or next to it.
MOD_VOY_HELP_HOLD_SELL: Sell sells straight from the hold, where the bank could sell: at a market or beside one, at that market's price.
MOD_VOY_HELP_HOLD_SAVE: The hold is in the mod's save data. Take everything out before removing the mod, or it is lost.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_FAST_TRAVEL: Travelling to other hexes with ${groupName} is a sail: your ship must lie at the port you leave from, and it costs stores, wear and light for every hex of the straight run.
MOD_VOY_HELP_XP_FAST_TRAVEL: A fast-travel hop by ship counts its hexes as water.
MOD_VOY_HELP_FIRST_HEX: A hex you have never entered (once each; never under cloud)
MOD_VOY_HELP_DISCOUNT: Each Voyage level cuts the GP cost of hex travel by ${per}%. At your level that is ${pct}% off, up to ${max}% at 99.
MOD_VOY_HELP_NO_XP_REACH: Moves back toward land from beyond your ship's reach.
MOD_VOY_HELP_COMPASS_BANK: It works while it is in your bank.
MOD_VOY_HELP_COMPASS_POINTS: When a skill doesn't work where you stand (Mining, Woodcutting, Smithing and the like), the compass points toward the nearest place where it does.
MOD_VOY_HELP_COMPASS_PANEL: On the map, in the "You are here" panel: a locked skill's tooltip says what it needs, and a tap opens the skill's page.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_LAND: Skills work only where the land allows: trees for Woodcutting, water for Fishing, a town for crafting.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_SURVEY: Survey with Cartography to see what is around you.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_TRADE_WHERE: You can sell and buy only in or next to a town, port or market.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_COMBAT: Your skills start locked, so your first coins come from combat.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_COMBAT_LINE: The Combat line on the map lists the areas you can fight in from where you stand.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_PURSE: You have ${gp} GP for the road.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_COMPASS: It is in your bank and points to the nearest place where a locked skill works.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_SHARPEN: Levelling Voyage sharpens it; the shop sells a spare.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_NOTICE_RULE_WATER: You need your dinghy, or a bigger ship, to go on the water.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_NOTICE_RULE_BOARD: Board it by stepping onto its hex.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_NOTICE_RULE_ASHORE: When you step ashore, it waits where you left it.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_NOTICE_FAR_REACH: A dinghy keeps within ${reach} hexes of a coast it can land on.
MOD_VOY_SHIP_NOTICE_FAR_BACK: You are farther out, so for now it can only head back toward one.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_MANIFEST_LEAD: A ship's manifest says what she carries and where it is stowed. This is the book's: every page I wrote, and the leaf it is on.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_MANIFEST_REST: Resources, Places and the Guide write themselves as you go. Their bookmarks are at the edge of the book.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CHART_ALT: A pencil drawing of an old chart: a home coast on the west with a lighthouse on its cape, mountains and woods behind, a wide sea called the Long Run with a sixteen-point compass rose in it, and the far shores as islands to the east. A cartouche names it The Far Shores.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_NEW_PAGE: A new page in your journal: ${title}
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_FOOTER: Read about it in the journal: ${title}
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_FOOTER_NEW: A new page in your journal: ${title}
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CRAFTS_ANYWHERE: Anywhere at all: ${skills}. Each constellation still shows only from its own sky.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CRAFTS_RELAXED: Relaxed rules are on: gathering keeps to its ground and fire to dry land; every other craft works anywhere.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_FOREWORD_INTRO: If you are reading this, the Old Man has gone ashore for good, and the book is yours now.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_FOREWORD_WHO_BODY:
I was a ship's master once, on the long run to the far shores. My crews called me the Old Man, as crews do, and the name stayed when the ships were gone.
When my knees gave out I took a room above a chandler's and wrote down what the roads and the sea had taught me.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_FOREWORD_BOOK_BODY:
The first pages are the rules of the road, as I learnt them. The rest I left blank for you: what you find, where you find it, and the places you pass ([[tab:resources|Resources]], [[tab:places|Places]]).
The compass came with it. It knew the way better than I did, and it never told me more than I had earned.
The ${journal} key opens this book from any page, and closes it again; so does the book button at the top, by the potions.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_FOREWORD_BOOK_BODY_OF:
The first pages are the rules of the road, as I learnt them. The rest I left blank for you: what you find, where you find it, and the places you pass ([[tab:resources|Resources]], [[tab:places|Places]]).
The compass came with it. It knew the way better than I did, and it never told me more than I had earned.
The book button at the top, by the potions, opens this book from any page. A keyboard key can do the same: set one in Mod Settings, section Voyage.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_FOREWORD_YOU_BODY:
A book like this is no use in a drawer. It wants feet under it.
Write in it. Cross out what I got wrong. And when you reach a shore I never saw, put it down plainly, so the next one need not learn it twice.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_FOREWORD_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: the Old Man's pages are the rules of this mod in his words. Where he and the Voyage page disagree, the page is right and he is out of date.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CRAFTS_TITLE: Where each craft can be done
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CRAFTS_INTRO: I write this down so I need not learn it twice. The land decides what a hand can do: an axe wants trees, a net wants water, a forge wants a town.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_STORES_INTRO: Every hex walked or sailed costs bread, and every hex walked costs fire as well, rough or cold ground the most. Not every place will load a full measure.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_STORES_NOTE: Why the measure differs: a port loads straight from quay and chandler; in a town you haul it through the streets and pay the middlemen; a market sells food, and firewood is a hauler's trade; a farm spares what it can.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_SHIP_INTRO: A hull wears with every hex of sea, more in deep water. I keep her tight with timber and Pitch, as sailors always have.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_SHIP_NOTE: Why a ship burns no wood: fire was a crew's worst fear. The galley stove sat on a bed of sand, lit at set hours under watch. What a ship truly wore out at sea was its food and its own hull.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_HOLD_INTRO: What I would rather not carry, the boat can: a few slots of anything, reached only where the boat is.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_HOLD_NOTE: The hold belongs to the boat, not to me. If I leave her on a far beach, what is in her waits there too.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_INTRO: A hand or two along makes the road less lonely, but every one of them eats from my stores and sits in my boat.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRAVELS_INTRO: Every hex I cross teaches me something of the road. Water teaches more than land, and a hex crossed by lamplight more still.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRAVELS_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: walking on an empty belly or drifting home pays nothing, so the road can't be farmed.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CLOCK_INTRO: A voyage is not a wish; it is hours of rope and road. I set off, and the hexes come to me one at a time, each in its own good time.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CLOCK_PACE_BODY:
What carries me on land shortens every land hex: boots, the yak, the horse, the unicorn, each quicker than the last ([[ch:road|Boots, beasts and the signpost]]). On foot it goes so:
| Land | One hex on foot |
| Easy land | 6 min |
| Desert, hills, mountains, the bad, waste and cursed lands | 9 min |
| Snow and lava | 12 min |
At sea the hull sets the pace and the ground has no say:
| Hull | One hex |
| Dinghy | 5 min |
| Longboat | 4 min |
| Brig | 3 min |
| Galleon | 2 min |
- A hop between ports takes its straight-line hexes at that same pace.
> Night falls on each hex at its own hour, so a long voyage may set off by day and come in by lamplight.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CLOCK_WAY_BODY:
Setting off is the work I am doing, as fishing or chopping would be. The Set off window shows the hexes, the time, the cost and when I should come in.
- Each hex is paid as I enter it: its GP, its stores, its wear on the hull, its Voyage XP. Nothing is paid for the hexes not yet reached.
- The Voyage page shows the voyage under way. Stop here ends it on the hex I stand on and keeps every hex reached.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CLOCK_LAND_BODY:
Before setting off I may name up to three things to do on arrival.
- The first that can start, starts; if it cannot, the next is tried, and so on down the list.
- Whatever I was doing when I left is offered among them, so I can take my work with me to the far shore.
- Or I name nothing, and wait where the road ends.
> If none can start, the Voyage page says why, and I stand idle there.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CLOCK_ASK_BODY:
Start another task while under way and I am asked first: drop anchor and do it here, or keep sailing. Dropping anchor ends the voyage on this hex; the hexes reached are kept.
What the hex itself forbids is refused outright, with no question asked.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CLOCK_FOG_BODY:
No road is charted through the fog, so I chart it myself as I go. On the map a hex under fog, or one a chart has cleared, offers Explore there: the voyage surveys each fog hex ahead before it sails into it, at the pace a cartographer keeps.
- Every survey pays its Cartography XP, as surveying by hand would.
- The surveying is time on top of the passage. A small hex wants some minutes of looking, a deep one above an hour, and the Set off window says how long all of it should take at the least.
- If I may look farther, I can survey a hex or two beside the route as well: slower, but more of the sea is known when I come home. No farther than my survey range reaches, mind.
- The fog's hexes are paid as I reach them: GP, food and fuel.
> A hex my Cartography cannot survey, nor will by the time I reach it, bars the way, and the voyage will not set off.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CLOCK_AWAY_BODY: The clock keeps going when the game is closed. On my return the hexes have been sailed, the arrival task has begun in its turn, and the Welcome Back window tells where the voyage ended.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CLOCK_OFF_BODY: Timed travel is a switch in the mod's settings, on to begin with. Turned off, every trip is instant again, as the game makes it, and the beasts of the road make land hexes cheaper instead of quicker. A voyage under way ends where it stands.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_WEATHER_INTRO: My town keeps the calendar, and the land keeps to it. What a hex asks of me depends on the season as much as on the ground.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_WEATHER_SEASON_BODY:
The season is my town's. Each lasts three days, and it turns whether I watch or not, the game closed or open. Before I have a town it stays Spring.
- The panel on the map shows the degrees where I stand, the season and when it turns; the Voyage page shows the whole year.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_WEATHER_BANDS_BODY:
Every ground has its degrees, and the season moves them: Summer 8 warmer, Fall 4 colder, Winter 12 colder.
| Degrees | On land |
| −15 and colder | bitter: fuel ×1.5, each hex ×1.25 the time |
| −14 to 0 | cold: fuel ×1.25 |
| 1 to 19 | mild: as ever |
| 20 to 34 | warm: fuel ×0.75 |
| 35 and hotter | scorching: fuel ×0.75, a ration more, each hex ×1.25 the time |
- The sea asks nothing for its degrees: there is no fire aboard.
- The Travel Cost box names the coldest or hottest hex of the way, and what it does.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_WEATHER_HARVEST_BODY: In Fall, food loads a quarter better wherever it loads at all: half becomes three quarters, and three quarters becomes full.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_WEATHER_ICE_BODY:
In Winter the sea within two hexes of the Snowlands freezes, and Frost Island is joined to the mainland.
- On foot the ice is ground like the Snowlands, and costs as much.
- No ship sails onto it. A ship caught in it, at a quay or not, is frozen in until the thaw, and I may step off onto the ice.
- A voyage whose way crosses the ice as it forms or thaws stops where it stands.
> Standing on the ice when it thaws, I am brought ashore by the shortest way, for nothing.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_WEATHER_WIND_BODY:
One wind blows over the whole sea, from one of the six sides of a hex. Every 6 hours it turns a side either way, or holds.
| Sailed | A sea hex takes |
| With the wind | ×0.7 the time |
| Across it | ×0.85 |
| Close to it | ×1.15 |
| Straight into it | ×1.4 |
- The dinghy and the longboat feel half of it; the brig and the galleon all of it.
- It changes only the time, never what a hex costs, and land feels no wind. With Timed travel off it does nothing.
- The wind follows game time, so a voyage meets the same winds played or not, and Set off knows them ahead: its time is exact, and it says what the wind saves or adds.
- The panel on the map shows where it blows from and when it turns, and its arrow points where it blows.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_WEATHER_STORMS_BODY:
A storm is a patch of seven hexes born on open sea, three or more hexes from land. It drifts with the wind a hex every half-hour and blows itself out after 3 to 6 hours. They are seen on the map as grey hexes with a bolt, so I can sail round one or wait it out.
| Season | A storm each 6 hours |
| Spring | 1 in 10 |
| Summer | 1 in 20 |
| Fall | 1 in 4 |
| Winter | 1 in 3 |
- A sea hex entered in a storm takes ×1.5 the time and ×3 the hull's wear (3%, 6% in deep water). One hex in four of a storm pushes you a hex downwind: sailing back costs a calm hex of time, nothing more.
- A vessel lying at sea in a storm wears 1% each half-hour. A hex beside a port is shelter: a quay is safe.
- The panel on the map and its strip show a storm within 3 hexes; Set off says when a route meets one. With Timed travel off a storm still wears the hull, but costs no time.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_WEATHER_RARE_BODY: My town may bring a rare season. Nightfall, the Solar Eclipse and Eternal Darkness are night all season long. In Lemon season rations at sea go a quarter further. All of them keep Spring's degrees.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_WEATHER_OFF_BODY: Weather is a switch in the mod's settings, on to begin with. Turned off, there are no degrees, no harvest, no night from the season, no ice, no wind and no storms: every hex asks what it always did.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_ROAD_INTRO: A ship is no use on a mountain road. For the miles between the shores I bought what every landsman buys, one thing after another, and each one paid for itself.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_ROAD_MOUNTS_BODY:
The shop's Voyage tab sells four, in order: Sturdy Boots, a Pack Yak, a Riding Horse and, at the last, a Unicorn. Each wants a Voyage level, and all but the boots want the one before them.
- Each carries me over the land quicker than my own feet, and takes the place of the one before ([[ch:clock|The ship's clock]]).
- With Timed travel off in the settings, each makes every land hex cheaper to cross instead.
- The Voyage page shows the one you have. Hover over it, or press and hold, to see what it gives.
> The sea goes at the pace it always did: that is the ship's business, not the beast's.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_ROAD_SIGN_BODY:
From Voyage level ${signLevel} the shop sells one Crossroads Sign. Some places do you good just for standing there. Plant the sign at one you have found, and that good goes with you wherever you walk or sail.
- To plant it, stand on the place and press Plant here on the panel on the map.
- To move it, go back, Pick up, and carry it on to the next.
- A signpost on the map shows where it stands, and the pin on the Voyage page takes you there.
> Stand on the place it marks and you get its gifts once, not twice: the place gives them, and the sign stands aside.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_BILL_BODY: What each hull cost me, copied from the yard's own bills. A shipwright builds the next hull out of the last: the longboat wants the dinghy at the quay, the galleon wants the brig.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_BILL_WHERE_LONGBOAT: Built at a port from the dinghy
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_BILL_WHERE_GALLEON: Built at a port from the brig
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_BILL_BONES: Why Big Bones? The yard says ribs. I asked once, and never again.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_ROAD_SIGN_SHOP: Not bought yet: in the shop from Voyage level ${level}.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_ROAD_SIGN_CARRIED: You carry it. Plant it at one of the places below.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_PLACE_SIGNED: Your Crossroads Sign stands here: these are yours anywhere on the map.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_ROAD_MORE: ${n} more such places are still to be found.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_ROAD_NONE: You haven't found such a place yet. There are ${n} out there.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_PLANNING_WHERE_BODY:
From Voyage level ${planLevel}, Plan voyage sits beside Show on map on every page of [[tab:resources|Resources]] and [[tab:places|Places]], and in the popup that tells you a craft or a fight can't be done here.
The Voyage page then shows the plan: the nearest place of that kind by the way you can actually go, not as the crow flies, and how many hexes of land and sea lie between.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_PLANNING_STOPS_BODY:
The plan counts the food and fuel hex by hex, as you would.
- It says what is left on arrival and how much the hull will wear.
- When the stores won't last, it puts in stops at ports, towns, markets, farms and camps on the way and loads there from your bank.
> When nowhere on the way can load enough, it says so plainly. Believe it, and load before you go.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_PLANNING_CHARTS_BODY:
Planning is free. Making the whole trip in one go takes Navigator's Charts.
| Navigator's Charts | Voyage level | Price |
| Any port, once | ${level} | ${gp} GP and ${pitch} Pitch |
The Shipwright row on the Voyage page offers them while I stand at a port.
- With them, Set off takes you the whole way, stopping to load where the plan says.
- On arrival sets you to work the moment you get there: the craft you planned for, or a fight in the area.
- If the game won't let you start something there yet, a Slayer level short or the wrong damage type, On arrival greys it out and says why. The voyage still goes; you only arrive idle.
> A plan is only a plan. If something stops you on the way, you stop where you are, with the rest still on the page.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_COMPASS_INTRO: It does not show the way; it tells me how warm I am. The better I know the sea, the more it says.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_COMPASS_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: the compass only speaks when the map has nothing to say. A place you know is always the better guide.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_MAP_INTRO: A chart is only as good as the eye that reads it. Here is how I read mine.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_MAP_TINT_BODY:
A surveyed hex is tinted by its land: green grasslands, white snow, red badlands, and so on. The Legend in the panel names them all, and [[ch:lands|The lands and what stands on them]] says what each allows.
A hex not yet surveyed shows nothing new. Survey with Cartography to see what it is.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_MAP_PANEL_BODY:
The panel at the top left of the map tells me the land under my feet, its features and the place, if there is one. Its top line shows the hour while the stores apply: day or night, and when it turns.
- Weather comes next; its triangle folds it.
- Then my vessel: where she lies, a voyage under way or a hull ready at the shipyard, and what the stores hold. Its own triangle folds this to its first line, but stores running low still show. A planned voyage stands under it.
- {folks} With you, under the stores, names the Worker Folks who go along with me, and Crew opens their block on the Voyage page.
- A shaded band holds what the place offers. Trade and Combat say whether I can sell or fight here, and name the area. Trade's OK opens the bank, and an area's name its fight. At a port, Harbour opens its board of cargo for hire. The Crossroads Sign is planted and picked up there too.
- {folks} Folks here, in the band too, names the Worker Folks who stand on this hex. From three on, this line and With you give a count, with the names in the tooltip.
- Works here lists the skills this hex allows. Tap one to go to its page; hover over it, or press and hold, to see what is found here: which trees, rocks or fish.
- Locked here lists the rest. Hover over one, or press and hold, to see what it needs and the nearest place I know where it works; a tap goes to its page.
- Manage voyage opens the Voyage page; the book button opens this journal.
Tap the top line and the panel folds to one short strip: the land, then only what matters this minute, such as the stores, a worn hull, the night, a planned voyage and what works here. Each goes where it is about, and a chip that goes somewhere wears a thin ring: the stores to the Stores on the Voyage page (a blue ring and a plus where I may stock up), the hull to the vessel on the map, a skill to its page. Tap the strip's triangle or the land's name to open it again.
{folks} With Folks along, the strip has a chip with their number: hover it for their names, tap it for the Crew on the Voyage page. It turns red once the food is out.
> On a phone, hold the triangle, on the strip or at the top line, and the panel shrinks to a square with the Voyage badge; tap the square and it comes back as it was, strip or whole.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_MAP_KEYS_BODY:
On the map, the ${key} key brings me back to where I stand, like the map's own home button.
The key can be changed or cleared in Mod Settings, section Voyage.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_MAP_KEYS_BODY_OFF:
The map's home button brings me back to where I stand.
A keyboard key can do the same: set one in Mod Settings, section Voyage.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_MAP_KEYS_OPEN: From any other page, the ${map} key opens the map.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_MAP_MARKS_BODY:
Show on map, under [[tab:resources|Resources]] and [[tab:places|Places]], draws a gold border round every hex I wrote down and turns the map to the nearest.
The marks go when I move on or open the journal again.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LANDS_TITLE: The lands and what stands on them
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LANDS_INTRO: Every hex is one kind of land, and the land decides what a hand can do there. What stands on it, a river, a forest, a town, can add more.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LANDS_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: these are the rules, not the riches. Where each ore, tree and fish lies is for you to find, and it goes into [[tab:resources|Resources]] as you do.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LANDS_KINDS_BODY:
Once surveyed, a hex is tinted with the colour of its land, as in the map's Legend.
What a hex costs to cross is in [[ch:stores|Victuals and fuel]].
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LANDS_FEATURES_BODY:
The panel names a hex's features after its land: "Grasslands · Cliff, Holy". These are the ones a craft looks for.
Most workshop crafts also work one hex out from their place: see [[guide:grace|Grace: one hex out]].
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_LANDS_DRY: ${skills} work on any dry land, so they are left out.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRICKS_TITLE: A few tricks of the road
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRICKS_INTRO: Nobody told me these. I learnt them the slow way, so you need not.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRICKS_STORES_BODY:
Stock up at a port when you can: it gives the full measure. A town gives three quarters; a market three quarters of the food but only half the fuel; a farm, village or camp half ([[ch:stores|the table]]).
Every Voyage level makes room for more food and fuel.
With empty stores you can still walk easy ground. It earns no Voyage XP, but it gets you home.
{folks} Folks with you go hungry on empty stores, though, and hunger can kill them ([[ch:crew|Folks aboard]]).
Snow and lava eat fuel fastest. Stock up before you cross them.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRICKS_BOAT_BODY:
Put by 500 GP and 50 Normal Logs early, and an Old Hat: no one sails under a bare head, and the river gives one up to any rod sooner or later (an Adventurer who has no rod yet may go bareheaded). The dinghy is built on any coast.
The boat waits where you step ashore. Leave her where you will come back.
Fast travel between ports sails your boat, so she has to be at the port you leave from.
Beach her to mend the hull: logs and Pitch, which Firemaking gives now and then ([[ch:ship|The boat and her hull]]). Keep a little Pitch in the bank.
Below half her hull she keeps out of deep water, so mend her before a long crossing.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRICKS_NIGHT_BODY:
Travel after dark when you can: the fuel left over from a trip lights the way, and a lit hex gives 25% more Voyage XP ([[ch:travels|Miles behind me]]).
Light never takes the fuel a trip needs, so night is never worse than day.
At sea a lit night, once in a long while, turns up a Steersman's Chart ([[guide:stars|Steering by the stars]]).
Firemaking levels make the fuel go further; Astrology levels make the light go further.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRICKS_WAY_BODY:
Survey before you wander: the panel names only places you have surveyed. The compass points to the nearest place whether you have or not.
Many crafts work one hex out from their place. Stand next to the town if the town itself is busy with something else.
What you find is written under [[tab:resources|Resources]]. Search it by the item you want, not only by the rock or tree.
Voyage level 10 makes the compass count the hexes; level 25 makes it name the place ([[ch:compass|The Wayfinder's Compass]]).
For a fight far away, pick the monster in its area first, then take Plan voyage: the plan remembers which one.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_SETTINGS_TITLE: If the road is too hard
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_SETTINGS_INTRO: Not every traveller wants every hardship. The rules can be softened, one by one.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_SETTINGS_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: play the way you enjoy. Turning a rule off is not cheating; it is choosing your road.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_SETTINGS_EASIER_BODY:
All of these are in Mod Settings, section Voyage.
| Setting | What it does |
| Relaxed | Keeps gathering tied to the land and lets every craft work anywhere; fire still wants dry land, so Firemaking and Cooking stay ashore |
| Resource zones off | Every tree, rock and fish of a skill grows wherever the skill works |
| Combat, trade, provisions | Each can be switched off on its own |
| Night | Moved to suit your hours, or switched off |
| Weather off | No degrees, no harvest, no winter ice, no wind and no storms: every hex asks what it always did ([[ch:weather|Seasons and weather]]) |
| Timed travel off | Every trip is instant again, as the game makes it ([[ch:clock|The ship's clock]]) |
| Voyage rules off | Every lock is lifted at once; the map colours and the panel stay |
| Motion on the map off | The traveller and the vessel stand still on the map while a voyage is under way |
| Open the journal by its cover | The cover opens and the pages turn every time the book opens, not only the first time |
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_SETTINGS_KEYS_BODY:
A few keys save a lot of clicking. Each can be changed or cleared in Mod Settings, section Voyage.
They keep still while you type in a box, hold Ctrl, Alt or Shift, or have a popup open.
Esc closes this book from anywhere, as it closes a popup.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_KEYS_MAP: Opens the map from any other page
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_KEYS_CENTRE: On the map, brings you back to where you stand
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_KEYS_JOURNAL: Opens this journal from any page, and closes it
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_SETTINGS_WHY_BODY:
The world map is beautiful, and the base game lets you ignore it. These rules make it matter: where you stand decides what you can do.
Each rule follows the real world as far as a game allows: trees in forests, fish in water, forges in towns, food from farms.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LEAVING_INTRO: Every voyage ends somewhere. If this one ends here, end it with care.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LEAVING_WHAT_BODY:
Load your character without the mod and save, and everything of Voyage is gone for good:
- Voyage XP, the boat, her hold and all in it (packed cargo too), your cargo runs and your task, your stores, the fog your charts and rumours lifted, a voyage under way, and this journal.
- What you bought for Voyage: the boots and beasts of the road, the Crossroads Sign and the Navigator's Charts.
- The mod's own items in your bank: the compass, any Pitch, the empty sacks and crates, the Tavern Tales and Sailor's Rumours, and the charts, Prospector's Notes and the rest.
> Putting the mod back later starts it all from the beginning.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LEAVING_HOW_BODY:
- Deliver or drop your cargo runs first ([[guide:cargo|Cargo for hire]]): packed cargo never comes out of the hold, so what is still packed is lost.
- Then take everything else out of the hold on the Voyage page ([[ch:hold|The hold]]): those are your own items, and they come back to the bank.
- {folks} Put the Folks with you ashore ([[ch:crew|Folks aboard]]). Without the mod they would stay on the road, idle, until each is given a skill.
- Sell the compass, the Pitch, the sacks and crates and any charts if you want their coins.
> Everything else of the base game stays as it is.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_ADVENTURE_INTRO: In this country every skill must be bought, and I had nothing to sell. The first coins came from the sword.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_ADVENTURE_FIRST_BODY: Fighting needs you on the area's hex or next to it. Walk there before you pick a monster.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_ADVENTURE_NEXT_BODY:
Buy a skill whose land is around you: the panel's Locked here tells what each skill needs and where, and [[ch:lands|The lands and what stands on them]] lists it all.
Keep enough GP for the road to a trading place, where the loot can be sold. [[tab:places|Places]] lists the ones you know.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LIGHTHOUSE_INTRO: Every coast I ever left had a light on it, and so did every coast I came home to.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LIGHTHOUSE_LAST_BODY:
This is the last page I wrote. The ones after it are yours.
I kept the lighthouse for the end because it is what I looked for at the end of every voyage: one steady light, and a keeper who never asks where you have been.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LIGHTHOUSE_LIGHT_BODY:
There are lights on this coast still. Find them for yourself; that is half the pleasure.
When the road is long and the stores run low, turn for home before you must. A captain who comes back can always sail again.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_LIGHTHOUSE_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: thank you for sailing with this mod. The land is still being written, and there are more shores to come.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_LIGHTHOUSE_ALT: An ink drawing of a lighthouse on a rock, its light sweeping over the sea, with a small sail on the horizon.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GALLEON_ALT: A careful pencil drawing of a three-masted galleon under full sail, flags streaming forward, gunports along her side and a lantern on her high stern. A ribbon beneath her reads Patient Grace.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GALLEON_CAPTION: Patient Grace, the last ship I had. I drew her from memory, and every rope is where it was.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_UNICORN_ALT: A pencil sketch of a smug unicorn with her eyes shut, the captain's hat stuck on her twisted horn, an anchor on her saddle cloth and a butterfly by her nose. Arrows mark my hat and not sorry. A ribbon beneath her reads Her Ladyship.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_UNICORN_CAPTION: Her Ladyship, drawn from life, which was my first mistake. She ate the first try and has worn my hat since Tuesday. She carries me three times as fast as my own feet, so long as it is where she meant to go anyway.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_ASIDE_KNOTS_HEAD: Why speed is told in knots
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_ASIDE_KNOTS_BODY:
Saw a deckhand on the quay this morning paying a line out over the stern of his boat, counting under his breath, and it took me straight back to my first ship.
That is where knots come from. A sailor threw a weighted wooden board, the chip log, over the side on a long line knotted at even lengths, turned a little sandglass, and counted the knots that ran out before the sand did. The count was the ship's speed.
The line is long gone from most decks, but we still say knots.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_ASIDE_LIMES_HEAD: The lemons that saved the sailors
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_ASIDE_LIMES_BODY:
Bought a net of lemons at the market today without thinking, the way an old hand does.
On long voyages a crew once died of scurvy more than of storms: bleeding gums, aching joints, old wounds opening again. In 1747 a ship's surgeon, James Lind, gave twelve sick sailors six different cures, and the two who were given oranges and lemons got better far faster than the rest.
In time the navy put citrus juice in every ration, and that is how British sailors came to be called limeys.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_ASIDE_MILKY_HEAD: The night the sea turned white
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_ASIDE_MILKY_BODY:
Last night past the reef the water went pale all around us, a steady white glow from the rail to the horizon, as if we were sailing over snow. The crew went quiet. I had seen it once before, forty years ago.
Sailors told of these milky seas for hundreds of years, and people ashore called it a sailor's tale. It is real: the glow comes from living things too small to see, in numbers past counting, and one milky sea was even photographed from orbit, a glowing patch thousands of square miles wide.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_LEVELS_HEAD: What the years at sea gave me
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_LEVELS_BODY: Every few Voyage levels the sea taught me something new. These are the ones worth waiting for; the ticks are the ones you have. The mounts and the sign are bought, not earned: they are in Boots, beasts and the signpost.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_LEVELS_DISCOUNT: And every level, big or small, makes the road cheaper: ${per}% off the GP cost of travel. Mine stands at ${pct}% now.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_HIRE_INTRO: No master sails alone. Ashore they call them Folks; aboard I called them my crew, and I paid them on the nail.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_HIRE_START_BODY:
Buy the Trainee Licence in the shop, under Worker Folks. It brings your first Shift Slot.
Then hire a Trainee. Every hand of a rank you already keep makes the next one of that rank a fifth dearer.
The Hiring page in the sidebar is your muster board: who works, at what, and who is owed.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_HIRE_WORKER_BODY:
Every skill page has a Worker box. Pick a Folk there instead of You, then start the work as you always would.
On this map the Folk comes to the hex where you stand and works there, so it can do only what that hex allows, as you could.
A Folk holds one skill while you do another, and keeps at it while you are away.
To take a skill back, switch the box to You, from anywhere. The Folk stops when you start work on that page, and only if this hex lets you do it: otherwise it carries on.
A Folk that lost its job this way keeps it in mind where it stands. Pick it in that box again, from wherever you are, and it goes back to work on its own hex. Any other job means walking over to it first.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_HIRE_PORT_BODY:
On this map, signing a hand needs a town, the capital or a port, as Township does ([[ch:crafts|Where each craft can be done]]).
Every hand then stands on a hex: where it was signed, or where it was put to work. Its card says where, and on the map a dark ring with a number marks each hex where hands stand: hover it, or tap it, to read who is there. Promoting, dismissing, settling a strike, its gear and a new skill want you within a hex of it.
A hand can also come along with you, and be put ashore on a far coast to work there ([[ch:crew|Folks aboard]]).
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_RANKS_INTRO: A good hand is made, not hired. Each rank comes good more often than the one before, and costs more. The first rank works a little slow; the top two work faster and save materials.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_RANKS_TIERS_BODY:
Under 100, the produce rate is the chance that a try comes good. Over 100, the rest is the chance of a second batch.
Wages are by the hour of work, paid per action, failed ones too.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_RANKS_LICENCES_B:
Each rank needs its licence first: a Hiring level, coins, a dungeon cleared, and a few items besides.
Your best licence also caps the Shift Slots: 2, 4, 7, 10, then as many as you like.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_RANKS_PROMOTE_BO: A hand is promoted, not hired again. It takes the next licence, the hand's own mastery at 20, 40, 60 or 80, a diploma item, and 60% of that rank's next hire price. Promotion opens at Hiring level 10.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_PAY_INTRO: Pay your crew before you pay yourself. I learnt that one the hard way, halfway to nowhere.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_PAY_WAGES_BODY:
Wages come from the Payroll Reserve first, then from the bank. The reserve opens at Hiring 5 and holds more as the level grows.
A fresh hand earns 40% of the rank's wage. It rises to the full wage at that hand's mastery 99: seniority costs money.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_PAY_GRACE_BODY: An unpaid hand keeps working for 15 minutes of work, 30 from that hand's mastery 25. Put coins back in time and the debt is paid on the next action.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_PAY_STRIKE_BODY:
After the grace the hand strikes: the skill stops and the slot comes free.
Settling costs the owed wages and a severance, then a rest: 30 minutes for a Trainee, up to 8 hours for a Foreman. An apology costs three times the severance and skips the rest.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_PAY_EASIER_HEAD: If the wages are too steep
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_PAY_EASIER_BODY:
Mod Settings, Worker Folks, Wage difficulty: from No sweat (free, no strikes) to Evil hardcore (five times the wage). Standard is the default.
No sweat only puts an old strike or debt on hold. It comes back on a paid difficulty.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_PAY_NOTE: A note from the one who named the land: a hand who dies, on the job or of hunger on the road, freezes the slot for a day of real time. A thieving hand eats your combat food below 60% health, so keep some selected.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_TIPS_INTRO: Things I would tell a new master on the quay, if they would listen.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CREW_TIPS_OWN_BODY:
Do your signing while you are in port. To promote, dismiss or settle a hand later, go back to it: you must stand within a hex.
To put a hand to work on a far shore, take it along and put it ashore there. It eats from your stores on the way, by its rank: a Trainee half what you do, a Foreman half again ([[ch:crew|Folks aboard]]).
Fill the Payroll Reserve before a long voyage: wages run while you are away, and they do not wait for the tide.
Hands wear their own gear, never yours: the Gear button on each card.
A Foreman lifts every other working hand's XP by 3%, up to 15%.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_RESOURCES_TITLE: What I have found, and where
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_RESOURCES_EMPTY: Nothing yet. The first time I gather something somewhere, it is written here.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_SEARCH_NONE: Nothing about “${query}” in the journal yet.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_COAL_NOTE: Coal country is the first trip worth saving up for. The walk there costs dear; by boat it costs about a third less, so build one first.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_NOT_FOUND_YET: Not found yet, only ruled out.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_HEAT_CANVAS: Map. Arrow keys move it, plus and minus zoom, 0 shows the whole map.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_HEAT_HELP: Drag to move, scroll or pinch to zoom; the arrow keys move, + and − zoom, 0 resets. Hover over a hex, or tap it, to read it.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CHART_DROP: ${name}: a chart of one country. Use it in your journal, under Resources.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CHART_FREE: Voyage ${level}: a free chart. Use it in your journal, under Resources.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_PICK_INTRO: A chart marks the whole country of one find: every hex where it works. The heat map shows it, and the compass and the hints may use it. A chart is never undone.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_PICK_NONE: Nothing left to chart for this craft at your level.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CHARTED_LINE: Charted: ${count} hexes where it works. The heat map shows them in pale gold.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_ISLANDS_LEFT: ${n} of ${of} lands set foot on. The rest I know only by hearsay.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_ISLAND_ASHORE: I first stood on it at ${hex}.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_ISLAND_NOTHING: Nothing else here is written in this book yet.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_PLACES_EMPTY: No places yet. Fights, trades, ports, lands and discoveries are written here.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_PLACES_SEARCH_LABEL: Search by place, land, monster or drop
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GOLBIN_NOTE: Golbin. They spell it so in this country, and I gave up arguing.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GOLBIN_ALT: A pencil sketch of a golbin in a crooked crown, scratching his head, a small dagger in his other hand. Beside him the word GOBLIN is written at a slant, the BL struck out and LB written above it.
MOD_VOY_GOLBIN_GIFT_BODY:
You went looking for goblins and found him instead. Good. Forty years I drew that fellow in the margins, and not one of my mates ever asked who he was.
He picked my pocket in Golbin Village, the night I picked his. His purse was the heavier, and it rattled. I never spent a coin of it: a man ought to keep something back for whoever reads his book closely enough to laugh at the spelling.
It is yours now, with a little tar besides. Buy yourself a longer boat, fair winds to you, and keep one hand on your purse in Golbin Village.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_INTRO: A page is written the first time a rule stops me. The blank ones wait for their day.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_NONE: No lesson yet. The first rule that stops me will be written here.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_TERRAIN_BODY:
Today I took my tools to the wrong ground and got nothing for it. A craft works only where the land has what it needs.
The lock names the nearest place I know where it works. If I know none, it says so, and then I must survey or ask the compass.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_TERRAIN_POINTS:
Gathering wants the right ground: trees, rock, water, soil.
Making things wants a workshop: a town, a camp, a forge, a temple.
Poorer ground is slower, but the work still goes.
The whole table is in [[ch:crafts|Where each craft can be done]], and land by land in [[ch:lands|The lands and what stands on them]].
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_ZONE_TITLE: Each thing has its own country
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_ZONE_BODY:
The ground was right, but what I wanted was not there. Each ore, tree, fish, crop and mark has its own country, as in the real world: copper in dry red land, tin washed down rivers, mithril in the frozen north.
Every place I found something is written under Resources, and every place I came up empty, so I need not try twice.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_ZONE_POINTS:
Search [[tab:resources|Resources]] by the thing you want, or by what it gives.
Show on map marks every hex where I found it.
The stars are the same: each constellation shows only from its own band of sky, away from town lights.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_GRACE_BODY: I worked a craft one hex away from its proper place, at full speed. Some crafts reach a little past their town, mine or temple, the way a smith works in the yard outside the forge as well as in it.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_GRACE_POINTS:
Mining, Thieving, Smithing, Crafting, Herblore, Runecrafting, Alt. Magic, Summoning and Township reach one hex out.
Grace never reaches onto the water or under cloud.
The hex one out shares its neighbour's resources: a thief next to a town finds the town's marks.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_TRADE_BODY: Coins are no use where there is nobody to take them. I can sell and buy only in or next to a town, port or market.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_TRADE_POINTS:
The panel on the map says whether trade works where I stand.
Every trading place I stand in or beside is written under [[tab:places|Places]], and a market with what it pays well and little for ([[guide:market|Every market its price]]).
If I am ever stranded with nothing to pay my way, a wandering trader finds me.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_COMBAT_BODY: A fight happens where the enemy lives. I must stand on a combat area's own hex, or one next to it, to fight there. Dungeons and strongholds are the same.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_COMBAT_POINTS:
The panel's Combat line lists the fights I can start from where I stand.
Areas I have fought in are written under [[tab:places|Places]], with Show on map.
Walking away stops the fight.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_COMPASS_BODY: I found a compass in my pack the day I arrived. It points to the nearest place where a locked craft works, and says how warm I am: Hot, Warm, Cold or Freezing.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_COMPASS_POINTS:
It speaks only when I know no such place myself.
Levelling Voyage teaches it to count the hexes, then to name the place ([[ch:compass|The Wayfinder's Compass]]).
If I lose it, the shop sells another.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_STRANDED_BODY: I came to a place with nothing left to pay my way. A wandering trader found me, as one always will: nobody is left stuck for good.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_STRANDED_POINTS:
He buys at half price where there is no market.
When my stores can't carry me to safe ground, he walks me there.
Any honest way to earn coin, a fight, a pocket picked, a town's taxes, means I am not stranded.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_DINGHY_BODY: Nobody stands on open water without a boat. I build my first dinghy on the Voyage page, standing on a coast, from coin, logs and an old hat out of the river (an Adventurer with no rod yet may go bareheaded).
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_DINGHY_POINTS:
To board, I step onto the boat's hex; to land, I step onto a coast.
The boat waits where I leave her, so I had better remember where that was.
A dinghy keeps close to land; bigger hulls go farther ([[ch:ship|The boat and her hull]]).
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_ISLAND_BODY: I could see the island, but my hull could not land on it. Each island wants a hull of its own size, in the order its dungeons are meant to be met.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_ISLAND_POINTS:
Western Isle, Golden Isle and Frost Island take a dinghy.
The Cursed Isle needs a longboat, the Ominous Isle a brig.
I may always walk on and leave an island I am already on.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_LONGBOAT_BODY:
Today a shipwright at the quay made more of my dinghy: a longboat, with a short mast and a red strake. She rows four hexes out from land where the dinghy kept to two, and she lands on the Cursed Isle.
She took the dinghy's place at the quay with everything that was in the hold, and the hold grew with her.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_LONGBOAT_POINTS:
Built at a port from Voyage level 30, with the dinghy on your hex or next to it.
Still a small boat: board her or leave her on any coast, and beach her to mend the hull.
Twelve crates in the hold, and more with the levels.
The sea past four hexes from land is still not hers. A sailing ship is: [[guide:brig|The brig, and the boat on her deck]].
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_BRIG_TITLE: The brig, and the boat on her deck
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_BRIG_BODY:
I bought a brig today, at the quay, and I am two vessels now. She is a sailing ship: she keeps the open sea, five hexes out from land and under cloud too, and she touches land only at a port. My small boat rides on her deck, and that is how I get ashore anywhere else.
Standing on the brig with the boat aboard, and land within two hexes, I step onto the water beside her: I am in the boat, and she lies at anchor until I row back onto her hex.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_BRIG_POINTS:
Bought at a port from Voyage level 45; she ties up at that port's quay, and your small boat stays yours.
Ashore from a quay: step onto the port. Ashore anywhere else: in the small boat.
The boat lands where its own hull may, or where the brig's may while she lies within two hexes.
Leave either where she is. The map marks the brig at anchor, the boat on the beach, and you.
Two holds, both open while the boat is aboard. Mend the brig at a port; the boat on a beach, or on the brig's deck.
Fast travel sails the brig when she waits at the port you leave from.
The Ominous Isle wants a brig ([[guide:island|An island too far]]).
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_GALLEON_BODY:
The shipwright took my brig and gave me back a galleon: three masts, a high stern, two rows of guns. There is no sea she will not sail, however far from land and under whatever cloud, and the last far places are hers.
She keeps the brig's ways: ports only, and the small boat on her deck for every other shore.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_GALLEON_POINTS:
Built at a port from Voyage level 60, with the brig at the quay.
No reach to mind: any sea hex, under cloud too.
Twenty-four crates in the hold, the brig's cargo kept.
Mended at a port, like the brig.
She is the last hull. The rest is the sailing.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_FOUND_BOTH: You found a compass and a journal. Something is written inside.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_JOURNAL: It fills as you go: what you find and where, the places you have been, and a page for each rule the first time it stops you.
MOD_VOY_WELCOME_JOURNAL_WHERE: Open it with the book button in the top bar of every page, or beside Manage voyage on the map.
MOD_VOY_MILESTONE_HOLD: Hold: a new row of six crates
MOD_VOY_MILESTONE_PLAN: Plan a voyage: the route, the stops, the cost
MOD_VOY_PLAN_EMPTY: Choose Plan voyage on a page of the Captain's Journal, on a cargo run in the Hold, or in a popup that sends you elsewhere.
MOD_VOY_PLAN_ONE_GO: None: the whole way in one go
