MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CARGO_BOARD_BODY:
Stand on a port, or beside one, and the panel on the map offers its harbour board: cargo, notices and sea charts, each on a tab of its own (the last two in [[guide:board|Notices and charts]]).
Each port posts four to six requests a season (three days by the clock), each one:
- for goods you could make this day in a trade you know,
- bound for a port you have found,
- at least 12 hexes off by sea.
The harbours want most what a captain seldom troubles to make:
| Asked for | How often |
| The smithy's, the workbench's, the field's and the fire's goods, against any other trade's | 2× |
| Of each trade's goods, those you have never made, against the rest | 3× |
Yet the harbours talk among themselves, and ask the less:
- of a trade that makes but one or two things you can manage,
- for what one board has asked this season, at the next,
- for goods you have lately brought in, for a season or two, the quays being stocked.
> A port posts no cargo until a dungeon within 6 hexes of it has been cleared; its notices and charts it keeps all the same. Clearing one again may set a fresh request on a board close by. A lone pier that no sea lane reaches posts no cargo at all.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CARGO_TRADE_HEAD: One port alone trades with none
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CARGO_TRADE_BODY:
Back in my time a port lived by its neighbours: one harbour traded with another, and the board of each wanted goods carried to the rest. It holds so still. A board posts only for harbours you have found, so a captain who knows but one port finds its board bare, however rich the country round it.
Which is reason enough to go looking. Every port you find is a new name on every board within reach of it, and the farther it lies, the better the run pays.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CARGO_LOAD_BODY:
Goods travel packed, 50 to a sack or crate, and each fills one slot of the hold. Both are made in Crafting.
| Pack | Holds | Crafting level |
| Sack | crops, herbs, runes, ash, stardust | 10 |
| Crate | all else | 30 |
Load takes the request, fills sacks or crates from your bank and stows them in the hold of a vessel moored here.
- A harbour asks a new hand at a trade for a sack or two, and a master of it for a shipload.
- A request too great for one hold goes in loads: come back to the port that posted it for the next.
> The runs I carry stand under Errands, in the hold's block on the Voyage page, each with its port, its next load and the way there, and my task from the notices beside them. Three runs at once is as many as a captain can keep in mind.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CARGO_DELIVER_BODY:
At the port that wants it, the harbour board takes the cargo off your hands.
- Each sack or crate pays twice what its goods would sell for, and more for every hex of the run, in GP and in Voyage XP.
- Packed cargo stays aboard. It will not go to the bank, and it waits in the hold wherever the vessel waits.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_CARGO_DROP_BODY:
Any harbour board will take a run you no longer want.
- What is packed and aboard sells there for a fifth of its pay; the rest is forgotten.
> Better by far to deliver it.
MOD_VOY_CARGO_FAKE: Even though it looks like a harbour board, it definitely isn't one. Move along.
MOD_VOY_MARKET_NOTHING: Sold for nothing: ${what} fetch less than 1 GP here
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_MARKETS_INTRO: Every market pays well for some goods and little for others. These are the ones I have stood in; worked goods fetch 20 more in the hundred than raw wherever their kind is listed.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_MARKETS_LEFT: Anything not listed sells at its usual price. ${n} markets not yet visited.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_MARKETS_ALL: Anything not listed sells at its usual price. Every market is in the book.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_MARKET_REST: Anything not listed sells at its usual price. Noted when I first came here.
MOD_VOY_HELP_HOLD_CARGO: Sacks and crates packed on a harbour board sit in the hold sealed, one a slot. They can't be taken out: they leave only on the board of the port they are for.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRICKS_PAGE_BODY:
The blocks of the Voyage page are yours to arrange: take one by its title and drag it where you want it, into the other column too. On a phone, hold the title a moment first.
The small arrow at the left of a title folds a block you seldom need down to that one line.
Each device keeps its own arrangement. Reset layout, at the foot of the page, puts all back as it was.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_TRICKS_TRADE_BODY:
Make a stack of sacks and crates in Crafting before you set out: a board will not hand you a request without empties in the bank to pack it in.
Take cargo the way you were going anyway. The pay counts the hexes, not the hurry.
Sell where your goods are dear. The bank's Sell block names the best market you know for them.
Worked goods fetch a fifth more than raw wherever a market lists their kind: bars before ore, cooked fish before raw.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_MARKETS_PRICES_BODY:
Each market pays well for two or three kinds of goods and little for one or two; everything else sells at its usual price.
| Goods | In the hundred |
| The kinds it wants | 140–180 |
| The kinds it scorns | 60–80 |
| All else | 100 |
| Worked goods of a listed kind | +20 |
- The kinds are raw fish, ore, logs, crops, herbs, rune essence, gems, bones, stardust and ash.
- Worked goods are cooked food, bars and smithed goods, fletched goods and charcoal, potions, runes and crafted goods.
- The price is the market's on its own hex and the one beside it, wherever you sell from the bank.
> A port seldom wants fish, and a farm pays little for crops. Far from the sea, fish is a treat.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_MARKETS_LEARN_BODY:
A market's prices are learnt by going there: stand in it or beside it once.
- They go into this book under [[tab:places|Places]], with a ledger of every market known.
- In the bank, the Sell block says what this market pays for the goods in hand, and the best and the worst market you know for them.
> The panel on the map keeps no prices: look in the bank or in this book.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_NOTICES_TASKS_BODY:
Every port pins notices to its board, even one with no cargo to post: three a season, changed with its cargo every three days. They are of two kinds.
| Notice | Asks | Pays |
| A place to reach | set foot on a place not found, 10 to 30 hexes off, that your hulls can reach this day | half again the trip's cost by the common travel prices, and Voyage XP for every hex |
| Goods to bring | so many of something you can gather now, to this port or another you have found | twice what the goods would sell for, and more for every hex of the way |
- For a place, the board gives the way and a rough count of hexes, never the spot. Each place pays but once.
- Goods must grow or lie 8 hexes or more from where they are handed in, and only what you gather after taking the task counts, so a full bank is no help.
> A new hand at gathering sees few notices for goods: what he can manage grows close by every port.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_NOTICES_ONE_BODY:
A captain takes one task at a time. It stands with the cargo runs under Errands on the Voyage page, and on the board of every port.
- A place to reach is done the moment you stand on it, however you came there.
- Goods are handed in from the bank, on the board of the port the notice names.
- Any board will take a task back. The next one waits an hour: the harbours do not care for a captain who picks and drops.
> Now and then a task handed in brings a rumour with it.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_NOTICES_CHARTS_BODY:
A sea chart lifts the fog from one whole sea at once. The water is shared out among the ports, and each sells the chart of its own sea and of the seas beside it. A lone pier keeps none.
- The price is a tenth of what the hexes still under fog would cost to cross, rounded up to the hundred, so it falls as you clear the sea yourself. A sea with no fog left has no chart to sell.
- A chart lifts the fog and nothing more. Survey levels and Cartography XP are still earned the old way, hex by hex.
- Once in a hundred deliveries, a port's master hands over the chart of his own sea for the trouble.
> These are not Navigator's Charts, which let a planned voyage sail itself ([[guide:planning|Planning a long voyage]]).
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_CH_NOTICES_RUMOURS_BODY:
Work long enough within a hex of a town, port or market and you will hear things: a rumour for about every six days of work.
| Heard | The rumour | It looks |
| By a port | a Sailor's Rumour | to sea first |
| Anywhere else | a Tavern Tale | to the nearest place |
Read one from the bank, under Sell. It lifts the fog from the nearest place you have not found and the hexes round it, seven at most, and says how far it lies and which way.
- When no place is left untold, a rumour marks the country of some good under [[tab:resources|Resources]] instead.
- When that too is done, nobody has anything left to tell, and no more are heard.
> A rumour you have no use for sells like any trinket.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_CARGO_BODY: Every port keeps a harbour board, and beside its notices and charts it lists goods wanted elsewhere. I pack them from my bank into sacks or crates, carry them in the hold, and am paid at the port that wants them.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_CARGO_POINTS:
Sacks and crates are made in Crafting; each holds 50 goods and fills one slot of the hold.
I load at the port that posted the request and deliver at the one it names, with the boat moored there.
A port posts no cargo until a dungeon near it has been cleared.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_BOARD_BODY: The first harbour board I read had more on it than cargo: notices pinned up by anyone with an errand to give, and the charts of the seas round about, for any captain with the coin.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_PLANNING_BODY: Today I sat down with the charts before I sailed. A good master knows the whole way before the first rope is cast off: where she will stop, what she will eat, and what is left in the hold when she gets there.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_PORTS_BODY: Back in my time one port would trade with another, and so it goes still. With two harbours now on my chart, the board of each may want goods carried to the other, and every harbour I find after this is one more name on the boards.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_PORTS_POINTS:
A harbour board posts only for ports I have found, 12 hexes or more off by sea.
The farther the port, the better the run pays; worth the exploring ([[guide:cargo|Cargo for hire]]).
A port posts no cargo until a dungeon near it has been cleared.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_MARKET_BODY: Markets do not all pay alike. Each pays well for some goods and little for others, and I learn which by going there.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_MARKET_POINTS:
The bank's Sell block shows what this market pays, and the best and worst I know.
The ledger under [[tab:places|Places]] compares every market I have stood in.
Worked goods fetch more than raw.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_NOTICES_BODY: I took a notice off the harbour board: a place to set foot on, or goods to bring. The board wrote my name against it, and I was bound to it until it was done or given up.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_NOTICES_POINTS:
One task at a time. Give one up, and the board makes me wait an hour for the next.
A place to reach pays when I stand on it, by whatever road: half again what the trip would cost.
Goods to bring count only what I gather after taking the task ([[guide:board|Notices and charts]]).
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_CHARTS_BODY: A chart came into my hands, and the fog went from a whole sea at once. What lay under it was still mine to survey.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_CHARTS_POINTS:
A port sells the chart of its own sea and of its neighbours'.
The price falls as I clear a sea myself; a sea with no fog left has none to sell.
A chart gives no survey levels and no Cartography XP ([[guide:board|Notices and charts]]).
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_RUMOUR_BODY: Working by the harbour, I heard tell of a place nobody had charted. I kept the tale, to read over when I had the time.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_RUMOUR_POINTS:
Rumours are heard while working within a hex of a town, port or market: a Sailor's Rumour by a port, a Tavern Tale elsewhere.
Read from the bank, one lifts the fog from the nearest place not found and the hexes round it. A Sailor's Rumour looks to sea first.
It gives the way and the distance; finding the spot is still my own work.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_STARS_BODY: A clear night at sea, the lantern lit and the stars wheeling over the masthead. Among my papers I found a sheet I did not remember drawing: the night sky over these waters, every star where a steersman would want it.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_STARS_POINTS:
A Steersman's Chart turns up only on a lit night hex at sea, and seldom: about one in a thousand.
Read from the bank, it lifts the fog from the sea I am on, or the nearest sea when I read it ashore. With that sea clear it charts a resource country instead.
No light, no stars: an unlit hex, a hex ashore or the night set to Off finds nothing ([[ch:tricks|A few tricks of the road]]).
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_ADRIFT_BODY: Far out from any shore, with naught to pay the next league, the ship would bear me no further of her own accord. I lay adrift, at the mercy of wind and current, and learned what the sea gives to them that wait on her.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_ADRIFT_POINTS:
The current bears a drifting hull one hex in half an hour toward the nearest coast she may land on, and asks nothing for it, by day or night, whether I watch or no.
A passing ship will tow me to a port I know, for what the way would cost and half again, paid in coin on hand. There is no leaving a tow halfway.
While adrift, fishing is the only work there is. The catch goes to the bank, and now and then it brings help: there are odd folk out on the deep.
Once I lie by the coast, I am my own master again.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_WEATHER_BODY: The year turns out here as it does in town. When the season changed I felt it in the fire and in my legs: the same road asked more of me in the frost than in the green of spring.
MOD_VOY_JOURNAL_GUIDE_WEATHER_POINTS:
Every land has its degrees, and the season moves them: warmer in Summer, colder in Fall, coldest in Winter.
In bitter cold a fire eats half again its fuel and the snow slows every step; in the cold, a quarter more fuel.
Warm land wants a quarter less fuel. Scorching land asks a ration more for the thirst, and a rest at noon.
In Fall, food loads a quarter better wherever it loads.
In Winter the sea within two hexes of the Snowlands freezes. I may walk it, but no ship sails it, and a ship caught in it waits for the thaw.
One wind blows over the whole sea and turns every few hours. Sailed with it a hex goes by quicker, against it slower; my dinghy, rowed, feels half of it.
Storms drift with the wind across the open sea, seen from afar. In one, a hex takes longer and the hull wears three times over; a quay is shelter.
MOD_VOY_ITEM_TAVERN_TALE_DESC: A tale heard over a drink, of a place not yet found. Read it from the bank: it lifts the fog from that place and the hexes around it, or charts something you can gather.
MOD_VOY_ITEM_SAILORS_RUMOUR_DESC: Word passed along the quay, of a place not yet found. Read it from the bank: it lifts the fog from that place, a sea place when there is one, and the hexes around it.
MOD_VOY_ITEM_STARLIT_CHART_DESC: The night sky over open water, set down by one who steered by the stars. Read it from the bank to chart the sea you are on, or the nearest one from land.
MOD_VOY_CHARTS_INTRO: A sea chart clears the fog from one sea. Surveying is still yours, and the price falls as you clear the fog yourself.
MOD_VOY_CHARTS_FOOT: A port sells its own sea's chart and its neighbours'. Rumours are never sold: they turn up while you work near a town, port or market.
MOD_VOY_CHARTS_GIVEN: The port's master hands you the ${name} for your trouble: the fog clears from ${n} hexes.
MOD_VOY_RUMOUR_HEARD: A ${name}, heard while at ${skill}. Read it from the bank.
MOD_VOY_RUMOUR_TALE_TAVERN_1: A one-eyed cook swears there is a cove past the last lighthouse where the ice never closes, and a wreck in it nobody has picked clean.
MOD_VOY_RUMOUR_TALE_TAVERN_2: An old drover, three cups in, tells of a place up the hills where the road gives out and something still stands that nobody built.
MOD_VOY_RUMOUR_TALE_TAVERN_3: The landlord's girl says her grandfather walked there once, and came home with sand in his boots and would never say whence.
MOD_VOY_RUMOUR_TALE_TAVERN_4: A tinker pays for his ale with a tale: a place off the maps, an honest day's walk from here, if a man keeps the sun at his shoulder.
MOD_VOY_RUMOUR_TALE_SAILOR_1: A bosun's mate, wringing out his cap, swears the current set them past a shore no chart of his owns, and they could not put in for the swell.
MOD_VOY_RUMOUR_TALE_SAILOR_2: An old salt mending nets gives you a heading, a count of days and one word, 'landfall', and will say no more for any coin.
MOD_VOY_RUMOUR_TALE_SAILOR_3: The harbour pilot spits and says there is deep water out yonder where gulls gather and no fisherman will drop a line.
MOD_VOY_RUMOUR_TALE_SAILOR_4: A ship's boy, back from his first long run, will tell any who listen of the place they sighted at dawn and the mate struck from the log.
MOD_VOY_RUMOUR_TALE_ZONE: Every place worth finding is found, or so they say. But the teller knows where the good ground lies, and marks it in your book.
MOD_VOY_STAR_FOUND: Under the stars, a lantern lit: you found a ${name}. Read it from the bank.
MOD_VOY_STAR_READ_BODY: Clears the fog from the sea you are on, the ${name} sea: ${n} hexes still under it.
MOD_VOY_STAR_READ_BODY_LAND: Clears the fog from the nearest sea, the ${name} sea: ${n} hexes still under it.
MOD_VOY_STAR_READ_CLEAR: This sea has no fog left: reading it here charts a country you can gather in.
MOD_VOY_STAR_TALE: You lay the sheet over the night and the stars fall into place. Coast by coast, the sea around you comes clear.
MOD_VOY_STAR_TALE_ZONE: The sea here is charted already. But the steersman marked where the good ground lies along its shores, and you copy it into your book.
MOD_VOY_STAR_CLEARS: The ${name} sea: the fog clears from ${n} hexes.
MOD_VOY_STAR_NOTHING: There is nothing left this chart could show. Keep it, or sell it.
MOD_VOY_RUMOUR_CLEARS: The fog clears from ${n} hexes, about ${d} hexes ${dir} of you. One of them is a place you have not found.
MOD_VOY_RUMOUR_CLEARS_NEXT: The fog clears from ${n} hexes, right beside you to the ${dir}. One of them is a place you have not found.
MOD_VOY_RUMOUR_PLACE: Setting foot there, and surveying, are still yours to do.
MOD_VOY_RUMOUR_ZONE: ${name} is charted: ${n} hexes marked in the Captain's Journal.
MOD_VOY_RUMOUR_NOTHING: There is nothing left this rumour could tell. Keep it, or sell it.
MOD_VOY_RUMOUR_READ_TAVERN: Hear the tale out: it lifts the fog from a place you have not found.
MOD_VOY_RUMOUR_READ_SAILOR: Hear him out: it lifts the fog from a place you have not found, a sea place when there is one.
MOD_VOY_TASK_WAIT: You dropped a task not long ago. The board takes you again in ${m}m.
MOD_VOY_TASK_TAKEN: Task taken. It is shown on the Voyage page with your cargo runs.
MOD_VOY_TASK_HANDED_IN: Task handed in: ${gp} GP and ${xp} Voyage XP.
MOD_VOY_TASK_REACHED: You set foot there. Task done: ${gp} GP and ${xp} Voyage XP.
MOD_VOY_TASK_GATHERED: Your task has all it asks for. Hand it in at ${port}'s board.
MOD_VOY_TASK_REACH: Set foot on a place nobody charts
MOD_VOY_TASK_REACH_NOTE: The board marks the way, not the spot.
MOD_VOY_TASK_GOT: ${got} of ${n} gathered since you took it.
MOD_VOY_TASK_DROP_SURE: Drop this task? The board takes you again only after an hour.
MOD_VOY_TASK_REACH_LINE: A place you have not found, ${way}. The board marks the way, not the spot.
MOD_VOY_TASK_BRING_HERE: Gathered after you take it, handed in here
MOD_VOY_TASK_BRING_THERE: Gathered after you take it, handed in at ${port}
MOD_VOY_TASK_FOOT: One task at a time: hand yours in or drop it to take another. New notices in ${when}: this board's tasks and cargo change together, every 72 hours.
MOD_VOY_START_INTRO: Voyage ties skills to places, so where you start shapes your first days.
MOD_VOY_START_GAME_TEXT: Where the game starts you, by Old Village and the Farmer's Market. Best for a first character.
MOD_VOY_START_RANDOM_TEXT: Somewhere else on the map: land you can live and grow from, on the main coast or an island a dinghy reaches, with something to gather and a trader within reach. Everything else is the game's own map.
MOD_VOY_START_RANDOM_WARN: You're on your own: progress is not guaranteed.
MOD_VOY_START_ONCE: Chosen once for this character: it cannot be changed later.
MOD_VOY_SETTING_TIMED_HINT: Travel takes time: each hex is a timed action by its ground, your mount or your hull, paid as you enter it, offline too. Off: every move is instant, as before, and mounts make land hexes cheaper instead of faster.
MOD_VOY_CLOCK_CHANGE_WARN: Under way to ${was}, ${left} left. Setting off ends that voyage here (the hexes reached are kept) and starts this one from ${at}.
MOD_VOY_CLOCK_ARRIVAL_UNKNOWN: That ground is not charted yet: what can be done there shows once it is, so only what you are doing now can be picked.
MOD_VOY_CLOCK_ARRIVAL_NOTE: The first one that can start, starts. Each hex is paid as you enter it, and stopping keeps the hexes reached.
MOD_VOY_CLOCK_WHY_HERE: ${skill} can't be done on this hex.
